objects.original: A scalar projected-noise entry bundled as a progressive L² integrand.
objects.reconstructed: Put E=Euclidean R^I, S={x:||x||=1}, and V_j(x)=e_j-x_j*x, so [V_j(x)]_i=delta_ij-x_j*x_i. Write R_+=[0,infinity), and let lambda_T be Lebesgue measure on [0,T], transported to R_+ (the given comap of volume restricted to [0,T]). All time integrals below use this measure unless indicated otherwise. A ProgressiveL2Integrand eta on horizon T is a real process eta(t,omega), strongly progressive for the filtration, with (omega,t) -> eta(t,omega) in L^2(mu x lambda_T).
objects.evidence: AutoSamplingTheory/TechnicalLemmas/StochasticProcesses/SphereCoordinateSDE.lean:24; The record returned by the definition stores fun t omega=>c(t,X t omega).

domains.original: Finite Euclidean sphere, finite measure, nonnegative horizon and global nonnegative-time process.
domains.reconstructed: I finite with decidable equality; Omega measurable; filtration on R_+; finite measure mu; T>=0; sphere-valued X:R_+ x Omega->S; temperature a:R_+->R; i,j in I. Output is a ProgressiveL2Integrand(filtration,mu,T).
domains.evidence: AutoSamplingTheory/TechnicalLemmas/StochasticProcesses/SphereCoordinateSDE.lean:24; The local E,S abbreviations and finite coordinate instances are read with the definition.

quantifiers.original: For every X, temperature, i,j and selected T satisfying the construction inputs.
quantifiers.reconstructed: A definition for every I,instances,Omega,measurable structure,filtration,mu,finite-measure instance,T,X,proof of joint measurability,proof of strong progressiveness,a,proof of continuity,i,j.
quantifiers.evidence: AutoSamplingTheory/TechnicalLemmas/StochasticProcesses/SphereCoordinateSDE.lean:24; T is a construction parameter, not a fixed global cutoff of the process body.

assumptions.original: Sphere-valued X jointly measurable and strongly progressive; temperature globally continuous.
assumptions.reconstructed: Input proof requirements: X jointly measurable and strongly progressive; a continuous. T need not be positive and a need not be nonnegative.
assumptions.evidence: AutoSamplingTheory/TechnicalLemmas/StochasticProcesses/SphereCoordinateSDE.lean:24; hX,hProgressive,hTemperature exactly match; sqrt is the total real function.

conclusion.original: The returned process is sqrt(2 lambda(t)) [e_j-X_j X]_i and has progressive/product-L² proofs.
conclusion.reconstructed: The definition returns the record whose process(t,omega)=sqrt(2*a(t))*(delta_ij-X_j(t,omega)*X_i(t,omega)); its progressive field proves strong progressiveness of this process, and its memLp field proves membership of (omega,t)->process(t,omega) in L^2(mu x lambda_T). Internally c(t,w)=sqrt(2*a(t))*[e_j-w_j*w]_i and process(t,omega)=c(t,X(t,omega)); the other let/have terms construct the proof fields.
conclusion.evidence: AutoSamplingTheory/TechnicalLemmas/StochasticProcesses/SphereCoordinateSDE.lean:24; The continuity proof hProjected/hScale and compact coefficient lemma construct the two proof fields.

scopes.original: Literal all-time representative; L² certificate is only on the selected horizon; no temperature positivity.
scopes.reconstructed: The body specifies a pointwise process on all R_+ x Omega; the integrability certificate concerns [0,T]. This is a bundled definition, not a theorem asserting existence of a process with otherwise unspecified values. Real.sqrt is total and zero on negative inputs.
scopes.evidence: AutoSamplingTheory/TechnicalLemmas/StochasticProcesses/SphereCoordinateSDE.lean:24; The process formula has no if t≤T clipping, whereas memLp uses TimeMeasure.upTo T.
